Calcifications are assessed by morphology and distribution (BI-RADS 5th edition).
Morphology: typically benign calcifications (skin, vascular, coarse popcorn, milk of calcium, eggshell, dystrophic) do not require work-up; suspicious ones are amorphous, coarse heterogeneous, fine pleomorphic and fine linear or fine-linear branching (the most suspicious).
Distribution: diffuse (generally benign), regional, grouped (a cluster within about 2 cm), linear and segmental (the most suspicious, following a duct).
Here there are fine pleomorphic calcifications grouped in an area of about 1-1.5 cm: BI-RADS 4C (probability of malignancy between 50% and 95%; 4B or 5 are also acceptable choices). Proceed with vacuum-assisted stereotactic biopsy, checking with specimen radiography that the calcifications were sampled.
Ultrasound is not useful to exclude: microcalcifications are poorly seen and a negative ultrasound does not change the indication for biopsy.
On the MLO views there are dense bilateral axillary lymph nodes, partly confluent, without a clearly recognizable fatty hilum and with a similar appearance on both sides: on mammography they cannot be judged with certainty; after the diagnosis, axillary ultrasound (especially on the right) completes the staging.
Collection outcome: breast carcinoma, Luminal B subtype.
Calcificazioni fini pleomorfe o lineari: Grouped or segmental fine pleomorphic or linear calcifications: stereotactic biopsy, even if the ultrasound is negative.
Carcinoma mammario destro confermato da: Right breast carcinoma confirmed by biopsy, Luminal B molecular subtype (CMMD clinical data).
